introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: Two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Write the following acronyms in full as used in computing: SDLC, RAM, CPU, BIOS, POST. (5 marks)

(ii) What is a computer port? (2 marks)

(iii) Name three (03) computer ports and state a device that can be connected to each port you name. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Acronyms (5 marks, 1 mark each)**

| Acronym | In full |
|---|---|
| SDLC | Systems (or Software) Development Life Cycle |
| RAM | Random Access Memory |
| CPU | Central Processing Unit |
| BIOS | Basic Input/Output System |
| POST | Power-On Self-Test |

**(ii) Computer port (2 marks).** A port is a socket (an interface) on the system unit of a computer into which the cable or connector of an external device is plugged, so that data (and sometimes power) can pass between the computer and that device.

**(iii) Three ports and a device for each (6 marks, 2 marks per port)**

| Port | Device that can be connected |
|---|---|
| USB port | Flash disk, mouse, keyboard or printer |
| HDMI port | Monitor, television or projector |
| Ethernet (RJ-45) port | Network cable to a router, switch or modem |

(Other accepted answers: VGA port - monitor or projector; audio jack - headphones or speakers; PS/2 port - keyboard or mouse; parallel port - older printer.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) State what you understand by 'network topology'. (1 mark)

(ii) Draw labelled diagrams for a Star network topology and a Bus network topology. (4 marks)

(iii) State a difference between a star topology and a ring topology. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Network topology (1 mark).** A network topology is the way in which the computers and other devices (the nodes) of a network are arranged and connected to one another (the layout of the network).

**(ii) Labelled diagrams (4 marks, 2 marks per diagram)**

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

- **Star:** every node is connected by its own cable to a central device (hub or switch).
- **Bus:** all nodes are connected to one common backbone cable, which has a terminator at each end.

**(iii) Star compared with ring (2 marks).** In a star topology every node is connected to a central hub or switch, so if one cable fails only that node is cut off (but if the hub fails the whole network stops). In a ring topology each node is connected to exactly two neighbours so that the nodes form a closed loop and data passes from node to node in one direction; a break in the ring can stop the whole network.
